vignette: A 64-year-old man develops a right hemianopia. He can write a sentence but cannot read it back a minute later, although he can spell words aloud and recognizes words spelled to him. He cannot name colors but matches them correctly.

options.text: Left angular gyrus and Wernicke's area
Left calcarine cortex and splenium of the corpus callosum
Right calcarine cortex and left angular gyrus
Left optic tract and lateral geniculate body

explanation: Alexia without agraphia arises when a left occipital infarct blinds the right hemifield and the accompanying splenial lesion disconnects the seeing right occipital cortex from the left angular gyrus; writing, which needs no visual input, survives.
